title: External lab corpus for the 60 estimators: frozen design, hard study exclusion and a rules gate
intent: Freeze the external-lab design of spec section 4 (nine state groups, ~10k tracts, sources and versions, RULES.md recipe with its variants, per-component definedness) and implement the safety rails, so that the build is one reviewed command once -- and only once -- the organiser ruling and the Track A pre-registration allow any lab number to exist. This plan itself downloads nothing and computes no target.

spec.note: parsed at run time and cross-checked against the plan below; the plan is a machine-readable reading of the spec, not a restatement of it

rules_gate.decided_by: operator, recorded by the shared steward in orchestrator commit 901d5e3c8ee89eb9995e2adb15a3fee6c48b49ee
rules_gate.decision_verbatim: **Operator decision 2026-10-25 09:35Z (overrides every "until the organiser ruling" below).** No question goes to the organisers. Track B is allowed: fit the weights in the external lab, on geographies outside the four study regions with every study tract and its neighbours excluded, then apply only the learned weight vector to estimators computed from the provided data. Reference layers or equivalent copies are never computed on, joined to, or used to approximate targets for study tracts. Disclose the lab method in the writeup.

rules_gate.tension_recorded: the RULES.md sentences are quoted unchanged because it is the operator decision, not a re-reading of the rule, that authorises the lab; the mitigation the decision imposes is geographic separation with study tracts and neighbours excluded, and that no reference layer is ever computed on or joined to a study tract
rules_gate.operator_question: For the Bias Bounty Mapping Equity Challenge we would like to validate our estimators on an external lab: the same coverage-gap recipe applied to about 10,000 2020 census tracts in nine US state groups that contain none of the four study regions and no tract sharing an edge with one, using the reference layers that were removed from the participant package (TIGER/Line 2024 prisecroads, Microsoft US Building Footprints, USGS National Structures, CBP/ZBP 2023) plus the same Overture release. No lab value would ever be joined to a study GEOID or enter a submission artifact; the scored submission uses only provided data. Is building and reporting such an external lab permitted under the rule that removed reference layers or equivalent copies obtained elsewhere must not be used to recreate or approximate the targets, or is it permitted only as Best Bias Discovery documentation? May weights fitted on other US geographies using public TIGER/MS/USGS/CBP be applied to provided-data features? And are the provided `usfs_BuildingCount_sum` / `carbonplan_buildings` columns usable as features?
rules_gate.operator_question_note: retained verbatim for the record because the spec's own combined question also asks whether the provided usfs_BuildingCount_sum and carbonplan_buildings columns are usable as features; the operator answered the lab question and no question goes to the organisers

exclusion_policy.note: spec 4.1 as an executable policy: a candidate lab tract is rejected before any reference layer is loaded for it
exclusion_policy.study_county_source: COUNTYFP of the provided strata tract table per region (provided data only)
exclusion_policy.buffer_rationale: edge-sharing tracts are metres apart; an 8 km centroid buffer around every provided study tract is a conservative margin that a candidate must clear before it is kept
exclusion_policy.spatial_filter_must_be_outside_study: any state or county download must be justified by a county list that contains no study county and no county inside the buffer
exclusion_policy.county_exclusion_note: county-wide exclusion is off by default and measured, not assumed: the four provided packages touch 298 counties, so dropping every study county would empty AZ-R (Apache, Coconino and Navajo are all study counties), gut CA-F and TX-W, and contradict spec 4.2, which asks for the tracts of those counties that are *not in the sample*. The operative rules are the explicit GEOID exclusion and the neighbour buffer, both enforced per candidate before any layer is loaded

The lane records both texts and asks the organiser to resolve them instead of choosing between them.
